verdict.rationale: Cloudflare documents event-driven automation: Event subscriptions publish structured account events (such as a Worker build completing or an R2 bucket being created) to a queue, and Workers consume them to run custom logic. Cron triggers, Queues and Workflows that pause for external events add further trigger mechanisms. The 'rules' are imperative consumer code written by a developer, not a declarative rule definition, and the scope of the event catalog is not independently corroborated. Missing for 10: a declarative rule/condition-to-action definition layer, documented filtering or matching rules on events, and hands-on or independent corroboration of the event-to-action pipeline.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Event subscriptions allow you to receive messages when events occur across your Cloudflare account.

Cloudflare products (e.g., KV, Workers AI, Workers) can publish structured events to a queue, which you can then consume with Workers or HTTP pull consumers to build custom workflows, integrations, or logic.
Schedule cron jobs, run durable Workflows, and integrate with Queues
The ability to pause for external events or approvals
